The FCV now in effect. 'requires authentication' means the credential variables expanded on your workstation: keep the bash -c '...' wrapper.
true means the balancer is enabled, false means it is stopped. After the upgrade it should be true again.
'(no change)' instead of 'patched' means the value was already set.

No output means the file matches the cluster. Lines starting with - are the cluster and + your file. Lab example of a file out of sync: '-    image: percona/pmm-client:2.44.1-1' '+    image: percona/pmm-client:3.9.1' and '-    setFCV: true' '+    setFCV: false', plus a generation line.
Prints the cluster state and the running PSMDB version on one line. Wait for state ready and the version you expect.
Prints the running Percona Server for MongoDB version, for example the full X.Y.Z-N image version.
Prints the Operator image (percona/percona-server-mongodb-operator:<version>). The second command, when present, prints crVersion, the database image and the running mongoVersion.
Prints the value of the requested spec field(s) on one line. An empty line means the field is not set and the Operator default applies.
One row per cluster in all namespaces with the requested columns. Every cluster's CRVERSION must be within the range the new Operator supports.
Shows the CRD with a LABELS column. Helm-managed CRDs carry app.kubernetes.io/managed-by=Helm; that tells you whether to upgrade CRDs with Helm or kubectl.
One line per node with its name and architecture (amd64 or arm64). Every node must use an architecture the target image supports.
Prints 'Client Version:' and 'Server Version:'. The Server Version must be in the supported Kubernetes range for the target Operator version.
